source.title: Zero Sum Trees: A Survey of Results and Open Problems

accepted.question_text: Let m be a positive integer, and let c be an edge-coloring of the complete graph K_{m+1} by elements of the cyclic group Z_m. Must there always exist a spanning tree T of K_{m+1} whose m edges e_1, e_2, ..., e_m have total color sum 0 in Z_m, that is, for which c(e_1) + c(e_2) + ... + c(e_m) = 0 in Z_m?
accepted.context_brief: Zero-sum spanning tree conjecture for Z_m-colored complete graphs.

evidence.quote: Conjecture. In every Zₘ-coloring c of the edges of Kₘ₊₁, the complete graph on m + 1 vertices, there exists a spanning tree of Kₘ₊₁, say T, with edges e₁, e₂, . . . , eₘ satisfying ∑ᵢ₌₁ᵐ c(eᵢ) = 0.
